Another rare example of a truly ORIGINAL horror game that has the courage to propose a fresh gameplay approach that, to my knowledge, has never been seen before. Deformed can be best described as a survival horror that borrows a few game mechanics from Dark Souls. In this game you have to survive in a dark and filthy underground lab populated by horrifying monsters that look like the nightmares of an individual who had the misfortune to spend a weekend in Silent Hill. BUT, and here comes the novelty, instead of fleeing and hiding from them, you are forced to face and destroy them with firearms. The entire game is designed as a boss-rush against a cheerful team of deformed monstrosities. And if you die, you won't lose any progress, because everything you do is permanent, just like in Dark Souls. Regular enemies respawn, but bosses do not. Once they're out, they stay dead. The downside, of course, is that once you spend XPs they're gone forever. If you waste all of them in resources, you can't upgrade your character, and vice versa. You just have to stay focused and carefully think before making purchases, that's all. Overall, this formula works PERFECTLY! At the beginning you may feel lost and disoriented, but once you get the grasp on the core mechanics, this game becomes incredibly fun and rewarding. Blasting your way through the nightmarish lab with loud gunshots feels exactly as cool and satisfying as it sounds. For once, we are not forced to just run away like bunnies, on the contrary, we can show our enemies who is the true boss! And speaking of enemies, I immensely appreciated each one of them. They are scary, putrid, genuinely disturbing, and each one of them has its own set of abilities, so that each fight requires a different strategy that can be refined with each playthrough. And, again as in Dark Souls, you can choose to face them in any order you prefer. Each boss rewards you with an additional resource or ability that, guess what, may become essential to defeat another boss much more easily! Strategy, ladies and gentleman. This is a game that, rather than being cheaply and artificially difficult, forces you to use your brain and rewards you for that. It simply respects your intelligence, as every single videogame on Earth should do. And on top of that, this game also offers a surprisingly deep storyline, that even succeeds in making you wonder who the true bad guy is. Such storyline is narrated both through the gameplay itself, and through AMAZING cutscenes, whose incredible quality genuinely astonished me! Overall, a very nice surprise indeed, an amazing horror experience that I strongly recommend to all true gamers and to all horror lovers. Cheers guys!

The fact that this was only fun and fair after i lucked out getting the free vending machine voucher says a lot. The game's alright, The idea is peak, and even with inf ammo and heals i kept getting scared. Sadly there's so much wrong i just couldn't. 1. Lack of weapon options. Being forced to pick between a shotgun, an Uzi, and an AK isn't exactly the most exciting thing. (tho the double Uzi is sick.) 2. Lack of direction. There is no map, which would be fine normally considering the map's small size. That is, if i wasn't constantly being thrown into boss battles with 0 build up or warning aside from a slightly different door. 3. "Common" enemies. They barely respawn so bosses are your best xp option, and they make ZERO sound until attacking, and by then its impossible to dodge. Maybe you could slide it off, but i can't considering the fact that i'm jumping from the ear splitting noise they make. 4. The doctor. the game claimed that walking inside the door would trigger a BOSS. not the "point of no return" event. 4 buttons aren't a boss. I have no idea why Sarah couldn't just...crawl back??? losing my run because i was lied to isn't exactly fun. and this is a major reason why i'm down voting. Jankiness and flaws are fine, lying to my face and deleting my progress for believing you isn't. The game's still fine tho. Might return if it gets a QoL update. edit: Ok, so aside from having 3 major points ignored, i'm being painted as some illiterate moron. Since there was 0 effort to comprehend what i've wrote, ill simply copy and paste the answer instead of putting even more effort into a response. "the game claimed that walking inside the door would trigger a BOSS. not the ('point of no return event.')" This was never a hostile review, I have no clue why you choose to feign ignorance instead of accepting the fact that i enjoyed the game (hinted by multiple praise) and that these are just things that'd make it even better if properly dealt with. I even said i'm willing to return if the game gets these very simple fixes. Also i'm just gonna call out these problems quickly: 5. The hardest enemy is the interference. died multiple times to the monster due to the trip mines not letting me interact with them. 6. Dialogue. You have zero control over dialogue stopping and can only skip it. So good luck if you're a slow reader.

One of the most creative and atmospheric Indie-Horror game I've played in a while, If Resident Evil, SCP and Dark Souls had a baby it would probably looks like this game. The graphics, cutscenes and writing are great, I honestly didn't expect it to be this good considering the small team behind it, and I absolutely love the souls-like "pre fight boss cutscene" My only complaints are : - enemies can attack and eventually kill you while you're stuck watching a small cutscene or during the looting animation - the text font style and UI could be improved - smaller enemies attacks are a bit weird sometimes, its like their stinger got a magnet on your character no matter how fast you run , overall , some animations could be improved (bosses and enemies attacks/deaths) - you can fall off the map in certain sections of the game I believe with the right amount of money all of this could be fixed and a sequel of this game could be made / what players need, giving the developers the reputation they deserve and eventually inspiring a new horror genre.

Got 1 of 3 endings and I feel pretty confident I can review the game at this point. Boy, this is a weird one. I initially thought it was a ♥♥♥♥-post, and the reviews really kind of make it seem sketchy. I can tell you that this is actually a pretty good time. You gotta have a bit of a high tolerance for trial and error, though. The start is a bit rocky, but once I figured out better what the dev was doing it started to flow nicely. It's got that kind of 2010's Half Life 2 mod sorta energy to it. Dying is really not a huge deal, either, and as you progress dying can actually be a bit of a pressure relief from unlocks. The game has got some jank, yeah, but it takes itself seriously and I found it to be pretty creepy. I also played entirely with a controller. No complaints at all. I intend to try and get the other endings, but I'm stopping for now. I enjoyed the game and my time with it. I recommend it even at full price. It's a good time with replayability. I'll edit the review with my new thoughts at the top in the event I get the other two endings.
